title: Cisco ISE Profiler Probe Quality and Endpoint-Classification Coverage
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'Cisco ISE Profiler Probe Quality and Endpoint-Classification Coverage' only. Does not replace full NAC policy design or firewall rule authoring or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `network_exception_register.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `network_cisco_ise_profiler_probe_quality_and_endpoint_cl` (UC-17.1.55), SOC dashboard panel "Network — Cisco ISE Profiler Probe Quality and Endpoint-Classification Coverage", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:network_controls.

compliance.assurance_rationale: Art.21(2)(d) — access control. Profiler classification feeds access-control policy.
AC-3 (Access Enforcement) — profile-driven enforcement requires profiler health.
A.8.18 (Privileged utilities) — profiler is privileged-info source.

controlTest.positiveScenario: UC-17.1.55 positive (Cisco, ISE, Profiler, Probe, Quality): ingest synthetic events into `index=nac` sourcetype='cisco:ise:syslog' where `unique_endpoints`, `avg_confidence` grouped by `probe_type` satisfies `probe_failures` > 0, `rate_limits` > 0, or `avg_confidence` < 70 for 'Cisco ISE Profiler Probe Quality and Endpoint-Classification Coverage'.  Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row.
controlTest.negativeScenario: UC-17.1.55 negative (Classification Coverage): ingest benign `nac` / `cisco:ise:syslog` events where `probe_type` stays below `probe_failures` > 0, `rate_limits` > 0, or `avg_confidence` < 70, or exclude the test entity via `network_exception_register.csv`. Variant 3 confirms zero alert rows for 'Cisco ISE Profiler Probe Quality and Endpoint-Classification Coverage'.

dataSources: ISE syslog `index=nac sourcetype=cisco:ise:syslog` *Profiler* category — codes `80001` (endpoint profiled), `80002` (endpoint reprofiled), `80003` (probe failure), `80004` (probe rate-limit), `80010` (profiler-feed update). Probes covered: DHCP, RADIUS, SNMP, NMAP, NetFlow, HTTP, DNS, AD, Active Probing. Field: `probe_type`, `endpoint_mac`, `device_type`, `confidence_score`. ISE OpenAPI `/api/v1/profile/feed` polled every 6h, written to `index=nac sourcetype=cisco:ise:profiler_feed`.
spl:
(index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:syslog" MessageCode IN (80001, 80003, 80004))
  OR (index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:profiler_feed")
| stats count, dc(endpoint_mac) as unique_endpoints, count(eval(MessageCode=="80003")) as probe_failures, count(eval(MessageCode=="80004")) as rate_limits, avg(confidence_score) as avg_confidence by probe_type
| eval health = case(probe_failures > 0 OR rate_limits > 0, "degraded", avg_confidence < 70, "low_confidence", true(), "healthy")
| where health != "healthy"
description: Identifies when Classification Coverage criteria fire for 'Cisco ISE Profiler Probe Quality and Endpoint-Classification Coverage' (UC-17.1.55) in `index=nac` sourcetype `cisco:ise:syslog`. Pipeline aggregates `unique_endpoints`, `avg_confidence` by `probe_type` over `the scheduled window`. Alert logic enforces `probe_failures` > 0, `rate_limits` > 0, or `avg_confidence` < 70. Title terms: Cisco, ISE, Profiler, Probe, Quality. Eliminates manual hunting for UC-17.1.55 conditions.
value: UC-17.1.55 helps teams contain Cisco, ISE, Profiler, Probe, Quality scenarios and reduce unauthorized access, segmentation drift, and NAC policy failures before incidents compound.
implementation: Confirm *Profiler* category at INFO. Schedule every 30 min, search window `-2h@h to @h`, trigger on count > 0.
visualization: (1) Per-probe health tile. (2) Confidence score distribution per probe. (3) Top-N: device types with low confidence.
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Certificate or EAP profile rollout** — Clients fail EAP-TLS during staged cert deployment for 'Cisco ISE Profiler Probe Quality and Endpoint-Classification Coverage'. Cross-check `FailureReason` and CMDB cert expiry.

2. **RADIUS/PSN maintenance restart** — Short auth failure burst while ISE node restarts. Match change window on `index=changes`.

3. **Guest or IoT onboarding surge** — Legitimate MAC registration spike skews `index=nac` `cisco:ise:syslog` baselines.

4. **Approved pen-test or scanner traffic** — Red-team exercises from netblock in `approved_scanners.csv` mimic auth failures.

**Suppression mechanism:** `network_exception_register.csv` keyed on `CallingStationID`, `NAS-IP-Address`, `valid_until`.
mitreAttack: N/A (data-quality monitoring — measures ISE profiler probe reliability, no adversary technique)
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• ISE Profiler enabled with multiple probe types active.
• `device_inventory.csv` for cross-reference.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable *Profiler* category at INFO.

Step 2 — Create the search
Search in `spl` field. Schedule every 30 min.

Step 3 — Validate
Provoke as above.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Dashboard "ISE — Profiler Probe Health":
• Per-probe health tile.
• Confidence distribution.
• Top-N low-confidence device types.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• **All probes show degraded** — PSN resource saturation; cross-ref UC-17.1.29.
• **DHCP probe absent** — DHCP relay not configured to forward DHCP to PSN.
• **NMAP probe disabled** — Either by policy (firewall) or PSN config.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (`Splunk Add-on for Cisco Identity Services` ([Splunkbase 1915](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/1915)).). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=cisco:ise:syslog, cisco:ise:profiler_feed into nac. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`avg_confidence, health, probe_failures, probe_type`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: ISE figures out what each device is — phone, printer, laptop — using several different methods. We check each method is working; if one is broken, ISE may be guessing wrong about what kind of device just connected.
